$comment: Vertex/Gemini failover-resilience knob PROPOSAL (lane F1, 2026-09-30).
These are PROPOSED values, not applied to the running gateway — the operator must
set the env vars / resilience settings and restart :20128 to activate them.
Citations are relative to the OmniRoute package root (v3.8.50):
<npm-global-root>/node_modules/omniroute/  (e.g. %APPDATA%/npm/node_modules/omniroute).
Vertex AI uses API-key auth, so the `apikey` resilience category applies.
No value here is committed to combos.json; see `combosProposal` below for the
combos.json delta (combos.json itself is owned by another lane and must not be touched).
NO per-LEG timeout config knob exists in omniroute v3.8.50. The closest surface is the
per-REQUEST fetch timeout, an env var read at
omniroute/src/shared/utils/runtimeTimeouts.ts:103-111 (FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS, default 600000).
A shared override REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS also covers it (runtimeTimeouts.ts:97-102).
Setting FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=30000 would cap every upstream request at 30s, but that is
per-request, not per-leg inside a combo. There is no per-leg timeout in the combo
executor; a true per-leg cap would require a code change, not a config change.
NO `idleTimeout` knob exists in the resilience settings (ResilienceSettings in
omniroute/src/lib/resilience/settings/types.ts:209-220 has no idleTimeout field).
The closest surface is the stream-idle timeout env var STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS,
read at omniroute/src/shared/utils/runtimeTimeouts.ts:112-120 (default 600000).
Setting STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 caps idle SSE streams at 120s. This is a stream
idle timeout, not a connection idle timeout.

failureThreshold.$comment: Original default 12 (apikey category). Proposed 3 so Vertex trips sooner under 400/429 storms.

resetWindow.$comment: Proposed 300000 (5min). Note the validation MAX is 600000, so 300000 is within bounds. Provider-level cooldown is separate: OMNIROUTE_PROVIDER_BREAKER_API_KEY_COOLDOWN_MS default 600000 (constants.ts:271).

$comment: When useUpstream429BreakerHints is true, the chat handler passes cooldownByKind to
the breaker (omniroute/src/sse/handlers/chat.ts:1507-1515):
rate_limit: 60000, quota_exhausted: 3600000.
The CircuitBreakerOptions.cooldownByKind is defined at
omniroute/src/shared/utils/circuitBreaker.ts:93 (Partial<Record<FailureKind, number>>).
NO knob named `cooldownAwareSkip` exists. The actual surface is `waitForCooldown`
(WaitForCooldownSettings, omniroute/src/lib/resilience/settings/types.ts:56-69),
consumed by resolveCooldownAwareRetrySettings at
omniroute/src/sse/services/cooldownAwareRetry.ts:38-68. When enabled, a 429
model_cooldown with a SHORT transient retry-after is waited out and re-dispatched
instead of skipping the provider. Caps: maxRetries <= 10, maxRetryWaitSec <= 300,
budgetMs <= 300000 (cooldownAwareRetry.ts:5-6,44-58). The 60-120s backoff maps to
maxRetryWaitSec=120. Also relevant: providerCooldown.minRetryCooldownMs (default 5000)
and maxRetryCooldownMs (default 300000) at types.ts:101-121.
PROPOSAL ONLY — do not apply; combos.json is owned by another lane.
If the operator wants the Vertex/Gemini leg to fail over faster inside a combo,
the combo entry for vertex/* should declare a shorter cooldown and a fallback leg.
No change is committed here; record this as a proposal for the combos lane.

suggestedCombosDelta.action: In the vertex/* combo entries, lower the leg cooldown to align with
suggestedCombosDelta.fallbackPriority: prefer gemini/* (OpenAI-compatible) over vertex/* when breaker is OPEN
